title: Python Functions: Arguments, Scope, Closures & Decorators
summary: Quick revision notes on how Python functions take arguments (*args, **kwargs, keyword-only), the default-argument pitfall, LEGB scope, closures, lambdas, first-class functions and decorators.

chapters.title: Functions as Objects: Mental Model
points: First-class functions: a def creates a function object bound to a name, so it can be assigned, stored in lists/dicts, passed as an argument and returned
Higher-order function: takes or returns a function, e.g. sorted(words, key=len), map(str.upper, xs), filter(None, xs)
Names are just references: g = f makes two names for one object; del f leaves g working
Callable check: callable(obj) is True for functions, classes and any object defining __call__
Interview Point: Why can a function be a dict value? What makes an object callable? Difference between passing f and calling f()?

chapters.title: Arguments: Positional, Keyword, *args, **kwargs
points: Parameter order: def f(a, b=1, *args, c, d=2, **kwargs) is positional, default, *args, keyword-only, **kwargs
*args collects extra positional args into a tuple; **kwargs collects extra keyword args into a dict
Keyword-only: any parameter after * or *args must be passed by name; def f(a, *, key) makes f(1, 2) a TypeError
Positional-only: parameters before / cannot be passed by name, e.g. def f(a, b, /, c)
Unpacking at the call site: f(*[1,2], **{'k': 3}) expands a sequence and a mapping into arguments
Interview Point: What is the difference between * in a def and * in a call? Why use keyword-only parameters? In what order are arguments bound, and what error appears for a duplicate value?

chapters.title: Default Argument Pitfalls
points: Defaults are evaluated once, at def time, and stored in f.__defaults__, not on every call
Mutable default trap: def add(x, acc=[]) shares one list across all calls, so add(1) then add(2) returns [1, 2]
Fix with the None sentinel: def add(x, acc=None): acc = [] if acc is None else acc
Defaults like time.time() or datetime.now() freeze at definition time; compute them inside the body
Immutable defaults (int, str, tuple, None) are safe; a default that is mutated or reused is the danger
Interview Point: Why does the list default persist between calls? How do you inspect a default? When is a mutable default intentional, such as a memo cache?

chapters.title: Scope (LEGB) and Closures
points: LEGB lookup order: Local, Enclosing function, Global (module), Built-in; first match wins
Assigning to a name inside a function makes it local for the whole function, so reading it earlier raises UnboundLocalError
global x rebinds a module-level name; nonlocal x rebinds a name in the nearest enclosing function; neither is needed just to read or mutate
Closure: an inner function that remembers variables from its enclosing scope after the outer function returns, visible in f.__closure__
Late-binding trap: [lambda: i for i in range(3)] all return 2; bind with lambda i=i: i
Interview Point: What is LEGB? When do you need nonlocal versus global? Why do lambdas in a loop all return the last value, and how do you fix it?

chapters.title: Lambdas and Decorators
points: lambda args: expr is a single-expression anonymous function with no statements and no annotations; best as a key=, e.g. sorted(users, key=lambda u: u.age)
Decorator: @dec above def f is exactly f = dec(f); it wraps a function to add behaviour
Standard wrapper: def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): ...; return fn(*args, **kwargs), so it works with any signature
Always add @functools.wraps(fn) to the wrapper, or the decorated function loses its __name__ and __doc__
Decorator with arguments needs three layers: @retry(3) calls retry(3), which returns the decorator, which returns the wrapper
Interview Point: Write a timing decorator. Why use functools.wraps? What does @retry(3) expand to, and how does stacking decorators order the wrapping?

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Functions, Scope and Decorators
points: Signature order: a, b=1, *args, kw, kw2=2, **kwargs; / marks positional-only, * or *args starts keyword-only
Mutable default fix: param=None, then create inside the body
LEGB: Local, Enclosing, Global, Built-in; use nonlocal or global only to rebind
Closures: inner function plus captured variables; fix loop capture with a default arg (i=i)
Decorator template: @functools.wraps(fn) def wrapper(*a, **kw): return fn(*a, **kw); stacked decorators apply bottom-up
